cards.0695: A woman of seventy-eight is in her own house at number twelve from first light until dark on Monday the tenth of January and empties a bowl under the bath tap in the morning and again at dark, stands in the doorway of a front room she has not sat in since July and looks at a folding step ladder standing folded against the wall under the window and does not go in, and is spoken to at her own back door by a lad with a note about a meter and says she cannot help him and does not ask him anything and he does not ask her anything about the ladder.
cards.0696: A man in his early forties is at his own unit from first light until dark on Friday the fourteenth of January and measures a pair of oak gates leaning against the back wall with posts already in the ground at a cottage, finds he cannot hang them on his own from a stool, has a scrap of scribing card in his pocket with twelve on one side and room on the other and a pencil behind his ear and does not write on it, and tells the man at the bench opposite he has lent his ladder out and does not say to whom.
cards.0697: A woman in her late forties is in a house she is clearing from first light until dark on Thursday the twentieth of January and sorts a front room without taking a blanket off a chair arm, speaks to a daughter with keys about what goes on a van and what does not, leaves a folded step ladder she sees on a landing where it is because it is not hers to move, and writes the figure for the job on her pad and puts no line for anything else on it.
cards.0698: A woman in her late fifties is in her own house at number nine from first light until dark on Monday the twenty-fourth of January and wipes the top of a fridge with six pads and crosses the first line twice, looks at an ash stool in her front room with nothing under it, speaks to her sister at number ten at her own door about a shed roof and felt and says in the spring and puts no day on it, and does not ask the man next door who borrows.
cards.0699: A woman in her early thirties is in her own house at number ten from first light until dark on Thursday the twenty-seventh of January and does not open a drawer with ply and tape and a pencil and a folded paper in it, looks at a shed roof from her own kitchen window and sees the felt gone at the front edge, speaks to the man from the coal yard in her own yard about the draught off the top of it and does not ask him for hands, and says in the spring and puts no day on it.
cards.0700: A woman of seventy-eight is in her own house at number twelve from first light until dark on Tuesday the first of February and squares a cloth over a taped box on the left of her kitchen table without opening it, stands at her own kitchen window and watches a gate standing back against a coal shed wall with a padlock hanging open in the hasp, speaks through the window to a woman with a clipboard at the gate who does not come down the path, and does not go into the front room where the ladder is.
cards.0701: A man in his early forties is at a cottage with posts already in the ground from late morning until dark on Saturday the fifth of February and sights a pair of oak gates against the posts on his own, finds the latch stile wants a pair of hands on a ladder, speaks to the man who has paid about the spring and puts no day on it, and does not write his number on the other side of his card.
cards.0702: A woman in her late forties is at a tip off the ring road and in her van from first light until dark on Tuesday the eighth of February and puts a bag of rags with somebody else blanket in it to one side without opening it, speaks to a man on the heap about a taped box with a folded bit of bag over its corner and does not open it, leaves a shut drawer under her passenger bench shut with her own bolster on the leads, and does not ask after a ladder.
cards.0703: A woman in her late fifties is on her own front path and at her sister house from late morning until dark on Sunday the thirteenth of February and carries a bit of shopping to number ten, stands in her sister kitchen and looks at a shut drawer without opening it, speaks to her sister about a sixty-watt bulb and a cold front room and says in the spring about nothing with a day on it, and walks home without going up the road.
cards.0704: A woman in her early thirties is in her own yard and kitchen from first light until dark on Thursday the seventeenth of February and switches her outside light on over her back door on a morning that is not Saturday and switches it off again, looks for a lamp at the end of the road and sees it on, speaks to her sister on the step about the ladder at number twelve which neither of them has asked about since December, and does not put a day on the spring.
